def run_case(name, mutate, cleanup, tokens):
        mutate()
        mutated_files = repair_files()
        records_before = [record_summary(path)
                          for path in records_in(REPAIR_RECORDS)]
        result = cli_activators("switch", ["--runtime", NODE_RUNTIME])
        text = ((result.get("stdout") or "")
                + (result.get("stderr") or "")).lower()
        records_after = [record_summary(path)
                         for path in records_in(REPAIR_RECORDS)]
        completions_after = read_completions(REPAIR_COMPLETIONS)
        units_after = repair_units()
        cleanup()
evidence.reason: The run_case helper captures mutated_files before invoking the CLI, then calls cleanup() immediately after collecting other post-CLI evidence without taking a post-CLI repair_files() snapshot. In the unsafe-metadata case, cleanup restores the original mode, so a controller write such as chmod 0600 to the 0666 drop-in is undone before any later file-preservation comparison. That lets the negative control pass despite a controller side effect. The finding identifies a live correctness gap in the test harness, not a proposal to add a new requirement.
